content: Hi, everyone, I am looking for the n-dimensional polar coordinate formula for radial decomposition to prove Sobolev inequality, Could someone point me to the place that states the radial decomposition of the Lebesgue measure on R_n in terms of the Hausdorff measure on the sphere?

Is this the statement you are looking for?

I don't think Mathlib has this yet

Weiyi Wang said:

Is this the statement you are looking for?

I don't think Mathlib has this yet

Right, Do u know where is this? thanks

I took this from Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions, which I am using as a reference to formalize related theory. The normalized Hausdorff measure docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure was introduced not long ago, and there isn't much lemma for it yet. This polar coordinate decomposition will follow from the general area/coarea formula (Theorem 3.8 and 3.10 in the same book), which is missing in Mathlib due to missing definition of Jacobian (#37295)

Alternatively, this formula can also be stated for docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere of the Lebesgue measure, and the integration formula should easily follow (though I couldn't find this in Mathlib either. There is a special case at MeasureTheory.integral_fun_norm_addHaar ?). The hard part then becomes showing the sphere measure coincides with the Hausdorff measure to make it useful in other contexts, and this is in development in #37310

I am working on the Morrey's Inequality, which is related to my final course project. Given the current gaps, I'll start by preparing the prototype on my branch, using 'sorry' and axiom for the polar decomposition and potential estimate steps that depend on your work.

Once your PRs are merged, I’ll update my code to use the official lemmas. is that okay?
Mathlib doesn't determine how your course project should go, so if you like this approach, then go ahead. Just be aware that sorry/axiom can accidentally introduce inconsistent theorems
